english: Esus gifted the Svartalfar, the winter court side of the elven civil war, with a breed of large panthers that were strong mounts as well as powerful attackers in their own right. A Nyxkin is a Svartalfar warrior who is bound to one of these panthers. The bond is so great that if either side dies, the other will as well. -- The Bestiary of Erebus
A Minotaur is a tall humanoid with the head of a bull. They are vigilante guardians, and outside of being unable to resist a fight they mind they are reliable soldiers. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Esus traveled to the dark hell of Agares only to find it deserted and in ruin. Disliking such a barren world Esus breathed life into the dust and a people half-formed appeared, shadows of a lost people. These people he named the Mistforms and he brought them into Erebus. Mistforms can attack people, but if left alone typically avoid any contact with men and go through their own patterns and habits with little regard for the surrounding world. These habits seem to have little purpose and many suspect they are dreaming they are in a world that no longer exists. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

The Stygian Guard are the silent servants of Hastur. They exhibit no attempts at communication and little evidence of thought outside of their ability to ruthlessly follow commands. When they aren't being commanded they seek out pools or other bodies of water and sink unmoving to the bottom unless disturbed. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

A mix of eagles and lions, griffons make loyal mounts and pets to those who are able to tame them. They enjoy dangerous flying so less reckless riders will probably only ride a griffon once. -- The Bestiary of Erebus

Sea Serpents can grow to be large enough to swallow entire ships whole and they release thousands of eggs during their mating cycles. It is only their frequent clashes with each other and the lack of food in their environment that keeps their numbers under control. -- The Bestiary of Erebus
[ICON_BULLET]Will abandon players that do not have the right State Religion, Civic, or Leader type

Use Pyre Zombies as expendable front line troops. They are stronger than Men-At Arms, if you include their fire damage, and when defeated will explode, damaging all units (enemy and friendly) within a tile of the zombie. They require both Fire and Death mana to train, and are not available to players of the Good alignment. They are Undead units, and so are vulnerable to the Undead Slaying promotion and the Destroy Undead Spell. The Overcouncil's resolution against Death mana blocks its members from training these units.

Magnadine's horsemanship is legendary, but he is more renowned for leading mercenaries to wealth and glory. Sellswords often rip up contracts to join his company. His charisma inspires loyalty that is worth far more than gold.

Baron Duin Halfmorn was a fearsome warlord during the Age of Magic. He hosted lavish banquets after his victories, where he and his generals feasted on the bodies of the vanquished. In time his generals' ambition grew to match his own. They turned on him in a bloody civil war. Duin won the war but lost his empire; he sat alone in the end, feasting on his generals' corpses. [PARAGRAPH:1]Ancient legends tell of Duin's cruelty, cannibalism, and worship of Camulos, but they do not relate his darkest secret. The God of Strife rewarded the Baron's devotion with the curse of Lycanthropy, yet let him control his bestial nature well enough to keep it hidden from the world. Duin was not the first werewolf, nor last, but was the greatest. [PARAGRAPH:1]The horrific Duin did die, as all mortals do, but would not be allowed to rest in peace. His soul fought for centuries in Hell, before returning to the world of the living. In a time of dire need, desperate mages performed rites to bring back the greatest, most feared general of history. [PARAGRAPH:1]Mortal magic may resurrect only the dead whose spirits linger in Erebus. Without divine intervention, it can never draw a soul back from beyond the plane. Camulos sent the Baron back on a mission to revive lycanthropy. Werewolves went extinct during the Age of Ice. Every infection in the current epidemic can be clearly traced back to Halfmorn himself. His true nature is now known, and rightly feared.

Duin is now a melee unit instead of a beast, so he cannot so easily be captured by Beastmasters, but he is still a werewolf. Living units that he slays, or even those that slay him, risk becoming infected with Lycanthropy. He is the Alpha Werewolf, who can dominate other lycanthropes to make them join his pack. Ravenous Werewolves are usually born rebellious, but they would not dare rebel against the Baron Halfmorn.

[TAB]The Frost Speakers, disciples of Mulcarn, were tolerated by most nations in the Age of Magic. They would pledge allegiance to no sovereign, but they did not speak sedition, either. Well beyond stoic in their demeanor, followers of Winter lost passion of all sorts. Initiation to this order involved bathing in icy waters overnight. Those who survived the 'baptism' usually had their outlook changed dramatically by it, without need of theological debate. [PARAGRAPH:1]These cold men now lead the armies of their god. Slow to adapt to their enemies' tactics, their strength lies in unflinching rationality, carrying out their plans unhindered by fear, ambition, or personal attachment. They will patch up wounded soldiers with divine aid of their god-king, but evidence suggests their compassion is something to be desired. More than once Amurite recon patrols have found badly wounded Illian warriors buried in the snow--occasionally still breathing.

[TAB]The protection of our national wealth demands that we restrict our trading, so as to prevent other nations from profiting from the work our faithful citizens have done. Any foreign power is a potential adversary, a vicious predator probing for weaknesses and biding its time. To hand it weapons and tools is to invite disaster. [PARAGRAPH:1]-Arian Kothrax, High Councilor, Steward of Inequity[PARAGRAPH:2]Trade has ever been the extinguisher of war, the eradicator of prejudice, the diffuser of knowledge. [PARAGRAPH:1]Is it not evident that the impoverishment and dependence of labor are abnormal conditions resulting from restrictions and usurpations, and that instead of accepting protection, what labor should demand is freedom. That those who advocate any extension of freedom choose to go no further than suits their own special purpose is no reason why freedom itself should be distrusted. [PARAGRAPH:1]-Henry George

A fire ship or fireship, used in the days of wooden rowed or sailing ships, was a ship filled with combustibles, deliberately set on fire and steered (or, where possible, allowed to drift) into an enemy fleet, in order to destroy ships, or to create panic and make the enemy break formation. Ships used as fire ships were usually old and worn out or purpose-built inexpensive vessels. An explosion ship or hellburner was a variation on the fire ship, intended to cause damage by blowing up in proximity to enemy ships.

Fire Ships are cheap expendable alternatives to more conventional naval combat, and a good way to get rid of otherwise obsolete vessels. When defeated they will explode, damaging all units (enemy and friendly) nearby. They can be produded through either arcane or mundane means, using either Fire Mana or Gunpowder.

Sarabride outlaws magic entirely and has an army of witch hunters specifically trained to kill mages. She also has a formidable force of cannons and steampunk style riflemen and pistoleers. Unknown to most, a small group of true angels of Bhall serve, guard and protect her.

No mortals are better trained than Witch Hunters for the task of protecting society from rogue sorcerers. Unfortunately, they tend to be cruel and corrupt. Even honest ones are often overzealous, failing to distinguish between good and evil uses of magic and more willing to condemn a hundred innocents than let one guilty party go free. Employing them especially angers those leaders whose political power depends upon arcane might.
Enlist the Nightwatch: A Nightwatch unit is provided to every member who pays, and the state religion requirement for training them is waived.
Enlist the Radiant Guard: A Radiant Guard unit is provided to every member, and the state religion requirement for training them is waived.
Diplomatic Victory for the Dark Magistrate
As Primus Inter Pares, you can choose a Resolution to put forward for a vote.
Our arrangement bought you but a little time. I now come to collect your soul.

Description: New alliances ignite a religious war in the mountains of Tempus Mor. [NEWLINE]Membership in the Undercouncil or Overcouncil cannot be changed. Victory requires eliminating the members of the opposing council. [NEWLINE]Requires: Into the Desert.

Description: Dain means to pass the trials of the Cave of Ancestors. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: This is a dungeon adventure. You control one unit through the challenges of the scenario and if that unit dies you lose.

[ICON_BULLET]The Compact allows the gods and their direct agents free reign over their own worshipers, but severely limits their interactions with the rest of Erebus. Demons bound by The Compact can move freely in hell, but cannot enter Erebus proper except in lands held by their team or by the Ashen Veil.

[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Special Rules: You do not control only one civilization, but cycle through to take control of every member of your team each turn. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Requires: Completion of The Black Tower, The Cult, and Against the Grey.
And now, for something completely different. . .
Yes. Our troops need every advantage they can get. I never trusted our enemy's kin anyway.

The Mage Guilds are the Amurite Aristocracy. In most nations Royal Guards are drawn from the sons of the rich noble houses that own most of the country. The Amurites have no hereditary nobility. A few magic bloodlines may dominate, but it is illegal for those born of such lineages to ever learn who their parents are. Anyone with innate magical talent is raised by the guild, indoctrinated to believe that their own guild is the only family that deserves their loyalty. All the guilds teach their adepts to serve the nation as a whole, but most also instill a deep suspicion as to the motives of their rival guilds. Any Amurite that could be called an aristocrat must have arcane potential, and would have been trained as an adept as a child whether or not he ever advanced to become a Wizard or Archmage. Those with true talent prefer the more honorable path of a cloistered wizard, but many who would be considered gifted mages in other lands still fail the Amurite's rigorous Trials. These must find some other way to serve their Guild, and to protect their nation from less scrupulous sorcerers.

Arcane Guards require the Aristocracy civic to build, and will leave you if you change civics-so don't bother building them if you plan to change government civics soon. They are very nice units if you meet the requirements, however, as they have the ability to learn any Mage-level spell and have no level requiements. Like normal Royal Guards, they can protect whole stacks against enemies with the Marksman promotion. They also start with the ability to cast Ring of Warding, to protect cities from enemy summons.

Few mortals have any hope of ever matching the strength of even the weakest Balor, although rare exceptions may rise to the rank of Demon Lord and rule over Balors of their own. Every Balor began as an angel in the service of a god, and either followed his master's path towards corruption or rebelled to fall on his own. All of the evil gods have Balors in their service, but most serve only Agares. The King of Hope has never created a single angel or demon, but has seduced many legions of true angels to abandon Good or Neutral gods and enter his employ.

Balors combine the powers of a [LINK=UNIT_PRIEST_OF_THE_VEIL]Ritualist[\\LINK] with strong melee combat abilities and affinities.[NEWLINE]They be trained by the Infernals, or summoned by any unit with [LINK=PROMOTION_ENTROPY3]Entropy III[\\LINK] or [LINK=PROMOTION_CHANNELING3]Channeling III[\\LINK] and [LINK=PROMOTION_AFFINITY_ENTROPY]Entropy III[\\LINK][NEWLINE]As True Demons, [LINK=PROMOTION_BOUND_BY_COMPACT]The Compact[\\LINK] forbids Balors to enter any portion of Erebus that is not already exceedingly corrupt. Those temporarily summoned by mortals can get around this limitation. [NEWLINE]There are Balors in the service of every evil god. Most were originally Angels of that god, but every Balor of Agares was originally an angel of a good of neutral god. Most Balors keep their original affinities.

Runewyns are [LINK=PROMOTION_MAGIC_IMMUNE]Magic Immune[\\LINK], [LINK=PROMOTION_WINGED]Winged[\\LINK] [LINK=PROMOTION_ANGEL]Angels[\\LINK] that can be summoned with [LINK=PROMOTION_FORCE3]Force III[\\LINK] or upgraded from [LINK=CIVILIZATION_MERCURIAN]Mercurian[\\LINK] [LINK=UNIT_ANGEL]Angels[\\LINK]. Either way, they receive a free promotion pick for every source of [LINK=BONUS_MANA_FORCE]Force mana[\\LINK] their owners control. Runewyns specialize in combatting magic. They are the only summon thay can bypass the defenses of a [LINK=BUILDING_RING_OF_WARDING]Ring of Warding[\\LINK]. Even when they loose the fight, they still destroy this and every other magically-maintained building in any city they attack. They also remove all of the spell sphere promotions and all magical effects from the units they attack (except [LINK=PROMOTION_AVATAR]Avatars[\\LINK]). Runewyns are strong against [LINK=UNITCOMBAT_DISCIPLE]Disciple units[\\LINK] and very strong against [LINK=UNITCOMBAT_ADEPT]Arcane units[\\LINK], targeting them in stacks of stronger units (except in cities).

Rather than upgrading to an ordinary Mage, Amurite Adepts with enough experience may become Wizards. A Wizard has all of the abilities of a Mage, but is slightly stronger in combat and begins with a Spell Staff and an extra free promotion pick for every source of Metamagic Mana its owner controls. An Adept still has to be at least 3rd level before it can be upgraded to a Wizard.

These fell beasts begin as ordinary animals, which [LINK=RELIGION_THE_ASHEN_VEIL]The Ashen Veil[\\LINK] corrupts and empowers through an unholy ritual requiring the sacrifice of many souls upon a [LINK=BUILDING_TEMPLE_OF_THE_VEIL]Demon's Altar. [\\LINK] They have limited duration; the Entropy that empowers them will consume them too, unless they continue devouring souls through either combat or [LINK=SPELL_BEAST_FEAST]further sacrifices[\\LINK], or the Entropy that empowers them will consume them too. Beasts of Agares are especially skilled at hunting down the holy warriors of other religions, especially Paladins.

The woods around the Well of Shadows is protected by the Widdershins Curse, confounding the sense of direction of all who wander near. A [LINK=PROMOTION_DEASIL_CHARM]Deasil Charm[\\LINK] or [LINK=PROMOTION_SHADOWWALK]Shadowwalk[\\LINK] render one immune.
A luonnotar his early 50's. He is plain, quiet, forgettable. He is immune to all magic. And has an incredible ability purge a person of all magical ability forever.
The unassuming Grigori hero combined the abilities of a Luonnotar and Runewyn, and has unequaled abilities in Force Magic.

Tomb Wardens are minor Angels whom Arawn (when he was God of Life as well as Death, before Sucellus claimed the mantle that first belonged to Nemed) tasked with guarding the passages that lead out from the Netherworld into Erebus. They are responsible for guiding new souls into the bodies of unborn babes, and helping children struggle through the first years of life in a world full of deadly diseases. Most continue to fill that role under the command of Sucellus, but many shirk their duties in order to assume jobs better suited for the Dullahan. These angels are as often found near the exits of Erebus as its entrances. They guide spirits of the dead out of Erebus, lest they be abducted by demons to join the great machine or hell of left to languish in an increasing state of corruption. Wardens specialize in slaying the Undead, but prefer to strike down potential Necromancers before they can raise such abominations. Most of what mortals know of Tomb Wardens come from tales told by grave robbers who narrowly escaped with their lives.

Tomb Wardens are strong against the Undead, and like the Undead can emerge to punish those who rob graveyards. They are most likely to defend Graveyards on Hallowed Ground, and their appearance in such graveyards extends the duration of the Hallowing there.

Created during the Age of Dragons, Djinn are strengthened by magical energy. They were Oghma's attempt to use the power of the other gods against them. Djinn are amorphous blue forms, though they usually choose to appear as humanoids, like men made of flowing water. In an environment without magic they become weak and sedentary. Their nature makes it impossible to imprison them in magical traps or bars, but in environments without magic they can be held in items as simple as tightly corked bottles.

Djinn are magic-immune summons with all the powers of Archmages. They are gifted affinity in one or two random spheres, based on your effective mana supply, allowing them to cast the greater versions of the spells from those spheres. The Tower of the Elements may grant them free promotion picks based on your effective supply of Metamagic mana.

An Adept with enough experience may be upgraded to a mage, putting him one step closer to becoming the even more powerful archmage. This upgrade requires the unit be at least 3rd level. Mages have access to stronger spells that Adepts. More importantly, they lock their natural affinity for at least once dominion of magic. This allows even more powerful versions of the spells in those spheres and causes the unit's combat strength to scale upwards with increading supplies of that type of mana.

A player may have only 7 Archmages at once. A Mage must be at least level 7 before it can be upgraded to an Archmage. Becoming an Archmage is the highest honor most Adepts or Mages could ever imagine. Politically it means being placed over the Mage Guilds of an entire nation. To reach this rank, Archamges must demonstrate the discipline and strength of will to fully master a dominion and cast the strongest spells their affinities allow. This talent also lets Archamges learn to wield weaker versions of every other spell sphere, with enough mana and experience. If an Archmage aspires to gain new affinties, there are 3 possibilities. He can use the Tower of Necromancy to transform himself into a Lich, at level 10 or higher. He can turn to The Ashen Veil, taking on an Unholy Taint and Making a Demonic Pact to share the affinity of a Demon Lord. Lastly, he can use the Tower of Mastery and a lot of experience to let him learn affinity for any sort of mana.

Moroi are men who drink the blood of vampires. This small taste vampiric power gives them enhanced strength and speed, and a feeling of invulnerability beyond that of their still-mortal form. The Calabim often make Moroi out of those they wish to sacrifice in combat. A Moroi who serves particularly well and survives the various suicide missions on which he is sent is occasionally gifted with true vampirism. Moroi can Receive this gift while only at level 3, whereas other must wait until level 7 before earning that honor.

[TAB]"Rifling" is the term describing the practice of putting helical grooves in the barrel of a "long gun" to impart a spin to the projectile. This spin greatly increases the bullet's accuracy at distance. [PARAGRAPH:2]Early long guns, like the Arquebus, were "smoothbores"; these lacked rifling and the bullets were significantly smaller than the barrels of the weapons. When fired, the projectile would bounce against the sides of the weapon's barrel, giving it an uncertain direction upon exiting the barrel. [PARAGRAPH:2]The Khazad began experimenting with muskets using grooved barrels and tighter-fitting projectiles halfway through of the Age of Rebirth, but mass-produced rifled muskets did not appear until the Age of Innovation after the Bannor reclaimed their old capital of Braduk the Burning and built the Foundry of Vengeance to honor Sarabride. The rifled musket was the standard infantry weapon during Matronae purges, while Cavalry officers prided themselves on their rifled pistols.

All of mankind, with the dread exception of the followers of the Undertow, have always strongly resented slavery, on the grounds that no being should be completely subject to another. Oddly enough, this view has never been put forth in regard to Man's fellow animals...-Selena Yera, Elven Mystic

[TAB]Only Agares knows the origin of these stones. They may be a pale reflection of the gems of creation or Agares's failed attempts to make his own. Regardless, they radiate powerful death magic and draw wraiths to them like silent beacons. During the Age of Magic necromancers were said to have turned the stones into powerful weapons for those that wielded them, but only during the Age of Rebirth were they made into weapons that could wield themselves. [PARAGRAPH]The Luchuirp shun demons such as Eidola, yet their Artificers have crafted abominations even more vile. The Enchantments that bring this golem to life also enhance the power of necromancy inherent in the material, creating soulless automata with affinity for Undeath magic. These machines have no wills of their and are not bound by the compact, yet the taint of hell remains within them and lets them summon Imps, Balors, and to channel the power of any Demon Lords with whom their masters have formed Pacts.

Instead of Eidola, the most evil of the Lurchirp command soulless machines whose building materials just happen to come from hell. The Compact did not anticipate Golems with powers like those of true demons, so these abominations are free to enter event Hallowed Ground. Sheut Stone Golems are harder to get than Eidola are though, as they require Sheut Stone mined from Hell terrain as well as a Sculter's Studio.

Frydwell have all the abilities of the Horse Archers that they replace, but no longer functionally identical. These most reclusive of elves now start with [LINK=PROMOTION_FOREST_STEALTH]Forest Stealth[\\LINK] (letting them to hide in [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST]Forests[\\LINK], [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST_ANCIENT]Ancient Forests[\\LINK], or [LINK=FEATURE_JUNGLE]Jungles[\\LINK]. ) and [LINK=PROMOTION_SUBDUE_ANIMAL]Subdue Animal[\\LINK]. They still require [LINK=BONUS_DEER]Deer[\\LINK] instead of [LINK=BONUS_HORSE]Horses[\\LINK].

Nyxkin get defensive bonuses, have no resource requirement, and can use [LINK=PROMOTION_FOREST_STEALTH]Forest Stealth[\\LINK] to hide in [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST]Forests[\\LINK], [LINK=FEATURE_FOREST_ANCIENT]Ancient Forests[\\LINK], or [LINK=FEATURE_JUNGLE]Jungles[\\LINK]. They have +1 Poision damage, making them stronger than normal Horse Archers, but do not have the ranged attack ability of the unit they replace.

Also called an Altar Dragon as it prefers sacrifices. They usually have a pool of blood nearby to drink from, and if their servants don't keep it filled they will usually find themselves added to it. Blood Dragons can take human form, and usually prefer to form of a dark nobleman, always with a goblet in hand. The roar of a Blood Dragon vomits up thousands of blood covered, biting, clawing, flying and venomous creatures, a torrent of creatures that are a mix between bats and scorpions. Blood Dragons maintain a collection of perfectly preserved body parts of their victims, skin, faces, organs, all displayed in a place the dragon can admire.

Coral dragons are not a single organism, but a collection of thousands of fist sized insect like creatures called Coralites all working together. They can separate and come back together freely. When they are together they have a breath weapon of white light that resurrects any newly dead (before their soul was collected) that it touches. Even to the point of breathing on a battlefield and raising all the fallen. Coralites occasionally get separated from their colony and have befriended humans as minor pets as they try to work out how to make it back. Coral Dragons collect precious stones, though they will occasionally leave them on the graves of those they respect.

These horned dragons glow with sunlight at all times, though they can control the intensity, from an angelic glow to a blinding golden light. Their breath weapon is a blast of light that burns the corrupt but won't harm the pure. Any ally touched by the light of a Dawn Drake is filled with incredible courage and hope. At dawn each day every Dawn Drake is fully healed from all injuries, mental, physical or magical and is broken free of any constraints that may hold them. They collect anything made of gold.

The largest of the dragons, Elder Dragons tower over castles and most giants. They are typically avoided by other dragons and most lair together in one remote location, the valley of seven pines, where the gods gathered to forge the compact. These dragons met Kylorin when he came to the valley, and allowed him to take the godslayer with him when he left. He occasionally returns and spends years with the Elder Dragons. Although all dragons are immune to mortal magic, Elder Dragons are even immune to the power of the gods (this was given to them as part of the compact, that they might enforce its commands). The roar of an elder dragon fractures creation, permanently leaving fissures of nothingness in the area. Elder Dragons don't collect anything, but they have a fondness for children of all species and are typically kind to them.

Also known as Fang Dragons or Lode Wyrms, these are the only flightless dragons. A Chthonic Dragon can pass through stone and are four times as heavy as it's significant size would indicate. It is quick on land, but when passing through earth it's almost instantaneous. It has no breath weapon, but it's bite easily cuts through stone and metal alike. Flesh and bone are little more than water to them. Chthonic Dragons can control a powerful magnetic field around their body, either attracting, or repulsing metal. Chthonic Dragon teeth, horns and scales are prized by enchanters and crafters. But priests of Kilmorph consider them sacred. Chthonic Dragons collect large gemstones and can be bribed for safe passage with a gem of unusual beauty.

These dragons never leave the sky, they fly endlessly, usually so high above creation they have little impact on the world, or the world on them. They are the fastest of the dragons and can rush over battlefields before most will know they are there. Their breath weapon summons a great wind, from gale force winds to a tornado depending on the dragons whim. These attacks are powerful but unfocused, as likely to damage the dragon's allies as its enemies. Feathered Serpents collect light and are mesmerized by the dappled effect of sunshine through leaves, firelight, rainbows and anything that glows or glitters.

Sometimes called Furnace or Inferno dragons. These large beasts are terrifying mixture of teeth, claws and scales. But their greatest threat is their fiery breath. It isn't just super heated flame that will melt stone and metal, but also a mucus that sticks to anything it hits and causes it to keep burning. Torch Dragon mucus is barely consumed by this and has been known to burn for days. Torch Dragon fire can also burn non-corporeal creatures like ghosts and spirits (some brave adventurers try to collect it for exactly this purpose). Unlike most dragons, Torch Dragons don't collect anything, but they are fond of beautiful music. [PARAGRAPH]Like most dragons, Torch Dragons slept through the Age of Magic, but when Bhall fell they awoke sensing that their goddess was under attack. The fury at the attack and the corruption of their dominion has led them to be very dangerous and unpredictable. They have no idea who is responsible for the pain they felt at Bhall's fall, but are ready to lash out at anyone they see in response to it.

These grey giants constantly exhume a green gas that is toxic to all life. Even entering a chamber where one sleeps will kill most people. Grave Wyrms collect bones like other dragons collect gold, decorating their lairs with piles of them that would make any necromancer envious. Grave Wyrms are immortal.

There were only ever a few Gold Dragons created by Amathaon. They were all beautiful, unique creations, whom he viewed as his children rather than mere weapons of war. To each Amathaon gave a unique gift. To Eurabatres, his first born, the model on whom all other dragons were based, he granted the power to speak and understand all languages, including those of plants and animals, the wind, fire, earth and sea. To all he gave the ability to change form, and to breathe a gas that causes amnesia and euphoria. Victims forget their former lives so they can start anew. Gold Dragons collect items of antiquity, they don't need to be magical or valuable but they have a fascination with forgotten eras and places. A flag of a country that no longer exists, or a statue of a man once notable but now forgotten, will delight them.

These glistening, black serpents looked to be fashioned from polished obsidian. They are fierce and temperamental. They love to fly at night and are swift and quiet fliers. They are thieves and collect items of high craftsmanship, from items as small as rings, to musical instruments, gravestones or statues. Anything that is beautifully made. Most assume that their glowing purple breath weapon is a disintegration beam, as that is the effect it appears to have on the target. But it's actually teleporting the target to a labyrinth within the nexus (which is almost the same as dying). Obsidian Serpents can see through all mirrors near them, and refuse to enter sanctified ground.

Also called a Chain Dragon, Demonic Dragon, or Dragon of the Depths. These horrific creatures dwell in bottomless pits. Like all the denizens of the lowest hell, they were not created by Agares but were seduced into his service. Most were originally Torch Dragons. Agares has chained a great rock to each of them that they must drag after them. They are capable of short flight even with this rock, but it requires great labor on their part. It is uncertain if Agares did this because he enjoys tormenting the powerful creatures, if they displeased him, or if it serves some other purpose. [PARAGRAPH]The dragon exudes an aura of fear that terrifies all life, even without being seen. Though it usually ignores life outside of its pit, it is drawn to suffering. A Pit Dragon's breath weapon is a dark vapor that corrodes metal, withers flesh and crumbles stone, but has no effect on the dragons chains or the great stone it is chained to. Unlike most other dragons, Pit Dragons don't collect anything.

Dragons are the greatest the weapons of the Godswar. They are all [LINK=PROMOTION_MAGIC_IMMUNE]immune to magic[\\LINK] and can scatter enemies in fear either by attacking or with a [LINK=SPELL_ROAR]Roar[\\LINK]. Most can [LINK=SPELL_TAKE_FLIGHT]Fly[\\LINK] and have a unique Breath weapon. Upon the signing of The Compact, most Dragons were locked away in an incorporeal realm. Some left bones as a testament to their former glory. In the Age of Rebirth, men have taken to [LINK=RELIGION_CULT_OF_THE_DRAGON]worshiping[\\LINK] the beasts in place of the gods who made them. Through the [LINK=PROJECT_STIR_FROM_SLUMBER]Stir from Slumber[\\LINK] ritual, they can awaken the weapons of the gods and try to recruit them to serve in mortals' wars. The ritual allows the appropriate civilizations to directly train Abashi, Eurabatres, Drifa, and Thalatth. It allows Dragons to be resurrected from their bones, or raised as Dracoliches. Most importantly, it reveals the locations of several types of Wyrmholds. Those lairs will then start generating dragons of their associated species. [LINK=UNIT_DRAGON_FANATIC]Dragon Fanatics[\\LINK] may visit the lairs to swear allegiance to a particular type of dragon, gaining affinity for their dominion and other promotions in the process, or may become converted to the cause of the first Dragon they hear Roar. Dragon Fanatics also have the ability to [LINK=SPELL_BESEECH_DRAGON]Beseech[\\LINK] a dragon to leave its lair and attack nearby enemies. The Fanatics get better results from exploring Wyrmholds, and may even recruit a dragon to join their player's control when running the Cult of the Dragon as a State Religion. [NEWLINE]The Dragons of the Depths are the least mobile dragons, as they are chained to heavy rocks at the bottom of their pits, but they are very powerful. Every Demonic Dragon once served another god before Agares corrupted it. Most retain affinity for their original spheres as well as for Entropy.

Sometimes called an Astral Dragon or a Ghost Dragon, they usually appear as spirits, though they can manifest physically if they desire. Rather than battle themselves Rune Dragons usually prefer to empower others to great action by binding their spirit with a host for a time. This gives the host great strength, fortitude, willpower and courage as well as the magical effects of skin as hard as a dragons hide, regeneration, immunity to hostile magic and a dramatically heightened power for any magical ability the host may already have. When physical, every scale of a Rune Dragon has been inscribed with an angelic symbol. They are long snake like dragons with wise, patient faces and can breath a silver light that destroys magic for a time. They only collect stories of the heroes they have helped and many are bound to material objects like a jeweled egg, or an ancient sword and if the need arises they make be awakened from that object to help the wielder.

Also known as the father of hydras (though there is no truth to it), Seed Dragons have three heads. They have no breath weapon but each head has a different venom, one causes a paralysis, another debilitating euphoria, and the third horrific pain. They also have a poisoned stinger on the end of their tail with a venom that causes death. Seed Dragons sleep in remote forest glades, plants grow quickly over them, completely obscuring them. Their presence increases plant growth for miles around. Many thick forests have a slumbering Seed Dragon at their heart, beneath a hill of growth or nestled within the roots of a great tree, though even those walking over them would never know. Seed Dragons collect unusual plants, taking seeds and pollen carefully from new plants to bring back to their glade. [PARAGRAPH]Seed Dragons were created during the Godswar by Sucellus, but he never participated in the war. So they were given to forests and areas sacred to him, to defend against those that would wander in and destroy the forests. But since no armies attacked Sucellus they had a peaceful existence, chasing off or killing the rare isolated enemies that would wander to close. Their peaceful nature (despite their threatening appearance) survives to this day and sometimes puts them at odds with Cernunnos's more bestial nature.

Scaled Dragons are the second largest dragon after the Elder Dragon. They can change their form, but not their mass and have been known to appear as great crocodiles or turtles, multi-headed dragons, lighthouses, great trees or small islands. They can also transform their body completely to water, and most commonly are in this form when they are underwater. Their breath weapon is a roar that can be heard for miles, and even further when issued underwater, that will bring help. This help can be from sea creatures, angels of Danalin or even the ocean itself. Scaled Dragons can instantly heal any injuries by pulling more water into their form. They collect shells and polished stones from along beaches and bring them down to their underwater lairs. A drop of their form (which appears as water), can allow anyone who drinks it to breathe water for seven days.

If the darkness is left to long, if centuries go by without a hint of light, it can manifest a cruel sentience. A form that swallows light and moves without sound. Shadow Dragons have two breath weapons, the first is a roar that consumes second is a dark tenebrous mass that strikes souls, driving them out of bodies and killing the victim. This leaves the husk of the body behind for just a moment before a shadow claims it, possessing the now abandoned body and using it to serve the dragon. Shadow Dragons are obsessive thieves and enjoy collecting anything that is loved by its owner and secreting it away to their lair.

Also known as Mirror dragons or Silver dragons for the reflective armor Junil has outfitted each with. Shield dragons protect a site or object and would never leave their charge. Most of these aren't holy objects of Junil, but infernal objects of great power that Junil wants to keep from getting out into creation. A Shield dragon protects the depths of Judicium. They do not need sleep, food or water. Their mouths are chained closed by Junil, and though there are rumors that their breath weapon is horrific, no one knows what it truly does. Shield dragons don't collect anything, their attention is focused on the object they guard.

Shimmering Dragons glow with a white, prismatic light, like glowing pearl. They are beautiful, elegant creatures and occasionally change to a beautiful human form. They are fast flyers, and though they are hesitant to ever attack, they are powerful fighters when they do. Instead of a breath weapon they sing, this can range from a soothing song that puts anyone who hears it asleep, to a sonic attack that will shatter glass and eardrums and crack stone. The tear of a shimmering dragon cures disease and insanity.

These massive war machines have spikes covering their body. Dead angels are stuck on the spikes as makeshift armor. The Siege Drake can fire these spikes if it desires, but they prefer charging and impaling victims on them. Warriors of Camulos prize these fired spikes as deadly spears that can easily pierce stone and metal. The roar of the Siege Drake calls back those it has killed to fight for it, including the angels that form its armor. A Siege Drake collects the bodies of those it has killed, especially the powerful. Its lair can have thousands of corpses in it, making the effect of its roar truly terrifying.

There was little cooperation during the Godswar. Even gods of similar disposition had occasional battles with each other, though not nearly as brutal as the massive battles that shook creation between opposed gods. One of those battles happened in the Scar of Falling Stars. Kilmorph's army was there, weathered and beaten from days of battle, when an army of Camulos drew close, led by the archangel Odio, who has never been defeated in battle. There was little hope for the children of Kilmorph. [PARAGRAPH]It was in that moment that the sky filled with light. Eldritch lightning rained down on the army of Camulos. Oghma had sent his Spire Dragons to aid Kilmorph in the battle. The dragons fought bravely, the night was a hurricane of wings, roars and death. Odio fought the dragons and the army of Kilmorph at once, and in the end he killed every last dragon. There are no Spire Dragons left in creation, they all gave their lives in this battle. No dragons were ever known to mate or lay eggs, but there are rumors that a nest of Spire Dragon eggs exist. If it is so, only Oghma knows where it is. [PARAGRAPH]Though they could not beat Odio in battle, Kilmorph sent the Anchors of Creation to bind him on the battlefield. And there he remains to this day, held fast and waiting until he can return to battle. [PARAGRAPH]The worshipers of Kilmorph have little love for flying things, but occasionally in their engraving or murals there will be an image of a thin, winged dragon soaring through the sky, lightning shooting from its mouth. This is their tribute to the dragons that died to protect them and our reminder that these graceful creatures once existed.

Vault Wyrm's are naturally a dirty brown color, but they encrust their body with precious metals and gems that makes them look like a gilded faberge egg. They have thin bat-like wings though many have become too heavy to fly. They can breath out a billowing cloud of gas that causes delirium and hallucinations to those that breathe it, this breath does not affect dwarves. They have acute senses and can feel the lightest steps by touch, hear the sound of the air brushing against skin, and smell past generations on a person. They hate thieves and will chase one to the end of creation for a single lost coin. Clever men will doom a victim by slipping a coin from a Vault Dragon horde into their possessions.

A blizzard always follows a Winter Wyrm, and the intensity of the blizzard grows with each Dragon in the group. Winter Wyrms can range from white to blue, with thick scales, sharp ridges along their back and a mane of grey fur. Once every 21 years Winter Wyrms awake and scour their arctic wastelands, killing anything they find. But outside of that brief time period they sleep so deeply not even attacking them will wake them and they can be killed (if you can get through their scales). Hollowmen and worshipers of Mulcarn have taken to protecting their lairs during their rest period, and hiding from them when they are awake. Winter Wyrms breath weapon is a ray of frost that is freezing cold and will put a few feet of ice on anything they breath on, usually entombing those alive that don't die to the immediate cold. Winter Wyrms collect anything that glitters, gold, gems, crystal or glass. worshipers of Mulcarn often leave elaborate ice sculptures around there lair and the dragons take care not to destroy them.

A Dracolich is an Undead Dragon, the product of Necromancy used on a Dragon instead of a human corpse. Dragons do not descend from Nemed and were never blessed by all of the gods, so the range of their gifts of affinity is limited. In general a Torch Dragon's affinity is only for Fire, so it could never simply learn Necromancy. A corrupt Grave Wyrm, however, could easily turn its natural affinity for Death towards Undeath. They would not do this for immortality, like most mortal archmages who become Liches, as they are innately immortal, but simply to gain the freedom to command death on its own without any constraints from Arawn. Other dragons could be raised as undead by external sources. A dragon's immunity to mortal magic makes them harder to raise, but they could be transformed through the necromancy of an evil Grave Wyrm, a Demon Lord, an evil artifact, or a curse like that which makes everyone who dies in the Deadlands return as undead.

Head of Clan Churel. Former King of the Calabim from the Age of Magic [PARAGRAPH]Churel was an ambitious and charismatic young man, adept in Spirit Magic, who became the lover of Alexis and convinced her to make him one of the first Vampires. He considered himself the King of the Calabim. For a period he and Alexis ruled their realm together. Alexis was open to sharing power with her consort, though it caused some strife with Flauros, and often allowed Churel to have his way when they disagreed. [PARAGRAPH]This lasted until Tristessa of Ashgate declared her city independent, overthrowing a weak vampire who had governed Ashgate for the Calabim. The city of Ashgate sat upon a passage to the Otherworld, for which it was named, from which the Archmage had summoned some truly horrible things to aid her revolution. The necromancer's power was such that even Alexis herself feared fighting her directly. Churel declared that Ashgate would be allowed to go free. When Alexis disagreed, Churel struck her in front of the royal court, leaving long bleeding cuts across her face. [PARAGRAPH]Alexis became a feral, raging monster. She attacked Churel and killed everyone who didn't flee from the throne room fast enough. She cursed Churel so that he could never again feed on the living, sothat he would starve to death. Then she dumped him at the edge of the Calabim empire and went off to kill every member in his clan before dealing with Tristessa. Churel lay beaten, spent and broken by the battle. [PARAGRAPH]Churel was maddeningly hungry, but unable to feed on the living. Desperate, he found that the undead had enough soul left to feed upon, without violating Alexis's curse. So he fed on ash bearers, broken men and worse. This has restored his power, but he is a corrupt dark creature, hideous in form with bending bones and a long grey body that bears little resemblance to the man he once was. [PARAGRAPH]The Calabim were quick to name his kind Graveleeches, insisting such abominations are something very different than vampires. Anyone to becomes a graveleech is forever shunned from society. [PARAGRAPH]Churel is a powerful creature; just a scratch from his claws is enough to kill. He radiates an aura of terror that few can resist. Since his curse Churel has raised some that sought him out or whom he found near death. They share his curse and are members of his exile clan. [PARAGRAPH]Most believe that Clan Churel is no more. Among the Calabim he is remembered only as the legend of what happens when Alexis is defied, but Alexis knows the catacombs that Churel haunts. When she needs him she will go command his clan's service. He is always eager to serve the queen who broke him, as he fears her far more than anyone fears him.

[TAB]Gaelan Sedracious was a lonely, awkward child. He was most at peace while alone, wandering the rosewood around his Amurite village, sometimes getting lost for hours. His village had a small school and shrine to Oghma. Though he loved learning, he suffered horrible bullying from the other children. One morning he came early to study, hoping to avoid the other children, but they caught him. Their bullying escalated to a stoning that left him nearly dead on the school floor. [PARAGRAPH]As an adult Gaelan was the head of an arcane cult called the Circle of Gaelan. They sought knowledge and were frustrated by the warnings and limitations of the more orthodox Laeran Cord. They ignored these restrictions and began summoning spirits and demons of the Mind in order to increase their power. They summoned and bound Gowlers, Endormillon, Haegtesse, Morphores and worse in their rituals. [PARAGRAPH]Each binding gave them new knowledge, but demons of the mind always had a price. They wanted some thought or memory from their summoner. The members of the Circle were forced to pay it but Gaelan had a way to avoid the cost. He formed a memory palace in Euphoria, a construct that had a copy of every precious thought and memory he had. When the demons consumed his memories, he could recover them. [PARAGRAPH]Gaelan wasn't satisfied with the lesser demons of Mind. He knew that there were more powerful true angels, created by Mammon himself that were intended to be angels of foresight and prophecy. Tired of just being able to know everything that has been, Gaelan wanted to know everything that was to come. [PARAGRAPH]These avatars were no longer spirits of foresight; they became the Roots of Fear after Mammon's fall. They no longer had the ability to see the future, instead they only saw horror, terror and panic. And they passed these visions to creation. Their impact on creation was felt by every living thing, but to meet one in person is more than the mortal mind can comprehend. [PARAGRAPH]The last act of the Circle of Gaelan was the summoning of a Root of Fear. The demon drowned them in their own personal terror and stripped their minds of anything close to sanity. But he tortured Gaelan, burning his body and mind until there was little left and then remaking him as the Burnt Priest, a servant of Mammon. [PARAGRAPH]As the demon explored the thoughts of the husk that had been Gaelan he found the secret his mind most closely guarded: the link to his memory palace. The demon followed the link to Euphoria where he was met by Caer. [PARAGRAPH]Caer and the Root of Fear battled in Euphoria. And nightmares spread to dreamers across creation as the battle occurred. The Root of Fear wanted the contents of the memory palace, but Caer shattered the palace rather than allow the demon to take it, allowing the thoughts and memories to spread to all dreamers. [PARAGRAPH]So many dreams were touched by the memories of Gaelan that some places have become fixed in the ethereal world of Euphoria, and continue to echo in dreams from people across Creation. Most prominent are a lonely but peaceful rosewood forest and a dark village schoolhouse haunted by cruel voices. [PARAGRAPH]After his transformation, the Burnt Priest moved into a small region called the Sunken Mire. The Sunken Mire was said to be gluttonous, swallowing all who enter it who don't revere Mammon. It became a base for the worship of the Undertow. Though strange creatures occasionally came in and out of the Mire, it was little threat to the surrounding lands. [PARAGRAPH]That was, until a group of adventurers entered the Sunken Mire attempting to purge its corruption. They were killed by the Burnt Priests thralls, but the Burnt Priest was angered by the attack and sent his forces to destroy Cuantine, the Bannor village whence the adventurers came. They slaughtered every citizen of Cuantine. [PARAGRAPH]After the Burnt Priest razed Cuantine, Order soldiers chose to test the legend of the Sunken Mire. They found and fought Endormillon, Haegtesse and Trow in the Mire as well as the Burnt Priests followers. They also discovered a Vault Wyrm, though no soldier stole even a single coin from the Wyrm so it left them alone. In a short but brutal, war, the thrall army was defeated and the Burnt Priest was killed by Gil-ganthor of the First Light. It is said that his sword was forever blackened where it touched the Burnt Priests blood.

Perpentach escapes death by transferring his mind into a younger host every few decades. He then kills the old body. But one of those bodies survived and dragged itself out of the pit of corpses it was dropped into. [PARAGRAPH]That surviving version of Perpentach wears a mask and has adopted the persona of the Red Jester. He is unwilling to go through the process to transfer his mind again, and terrified that Perpentach will discover him and come back to finish the job. [PARAGRAPH]His insanity and sadism leads him to running one of the most hidden (and sought after) underground performances in Jubilee, the Carnival of Knives. Although relatively small, with just a few acts, the artistry and cruelty are unsurpassed. The Red Jester uses mind control to force his performers (most of which are dead by the end) through shocking and beautiful displays. Such as the man who consumes himself, the failed escape, and the transforming man (who cuts himself into a bird type creature). Between performances the Red Jester prowls the back alleys of Jubilee to find and dominate new performers to replace those he lost. [PARAGRAPH:2]Perpentach[PARAGRAPH]Perpentach shuddered on the floor. He pinched his eyes shut and covered his ears in an attempt to drown out the outside world. What was going on in his mind was enough. The memories of a hundred lifetimes were pouring into him. Every memory was being recalled while the lens through which he viewed them was being reforged. He was inside a kaleidoscope of endless, tumbling, crashing scenes of joy and tragedy. [PARAGRAPH]He was Samual, an acrobat with a love of rum. Under its heady guidance he was calm and sure, dancing on wires or the backs of galloping horses with ease. But without it the world scraped against him like biting sand. In Samual's mind the world was fixed and distant, like a land across an ocean, things happened there but it was generally unchanged while he was consumed with the discomforts of his own life. [PARAGRAPH]That was a dozen lifetimes ago, another rebirth of Perpentach, another who had gone through this process and awoken as the Momus king. But Samual's thoughts and memories were included with all the others, and he still screamed for a drink. [PARAGRAPH]He was one of hundreds. One was Pau, a mute artist that had never spoken until the rebirth had unlocked his tongue. Osso, A murderer who began by avenging those who were abused, and when he ran out of victims became less picky about those he killed. Keter, a hateful underling who almost managed to assassinate Perpentach, until the Momus transferred into him before he died. Arn, a young boy prone to depression and thoughts of suicide. Vinner, A personable Foxman who always hated that the Momus rarely traveled. [PARAGRAPH]It was as the murderous Osso that he judged the weakness of fawning Keter, always taking abuse from Perpentach, crying in secret, comforting himself for years with imagined revenge while doing nothing about it. As Vinner he pitied the sullen Arn as family and few friends attempted to offer encouragement but eventually faded to their own lives and left Arn to the gray emptiness of his own. [PARAGRAPH]He was, at the same time, a traveler with a lifetime of stories from bold adventures and a timid recluse, tormented and beaten by the world until it terrified him. He was an enthusiastic womanizer, a scandalous uranian and an asexual sadist who was only excited by causing pain. [PARAGRAPH]He waited, but the spinning in his head never stopped. Instead he grew accustomed to it. He opened his eyes and saw the dimly lit throne room. It had only been minutes since he was standing here as he couldn't remember, there were a hundred voices in his head. One was probably that of his former life, but it was buried under everything that was new. [PARAGRAPH]The first epiphany from all of these new experiences wasn't wisdom, there was no universal lessons to be learned from all of these lives. Be good and good things will come to you no. The cruel will get what they deserve in the end no. There was no path to success or happiness, just empty ideologies adopted to provide comfort. Though the world was viewed through many lives, the world stayed the same. Where some saw hope, others saw despair. Where some were richly rewarded for their efforts, others suffered regardless of their choices. Life was random. [PARAGRAPH]It was so blatantly absurd that he couldn't help but laugh. Hundreds of useless intentions, sacrifices for no reason, endless ideals. The world was full of kittens all chasing imaginary strings. [PARAGRAPH]The laughter echoed in his head. He laughed until his lungs burned in his chest, his cheeks ached and his lips split and cracked. When he finally drew himself up off the floor he was gasping for breath, still overcome with small tremors of chuckles and twitches in his face. [PARAGRAPH]There was a reward for this process, a drink, Blood God wine. A treat he only allowed himself on these days. It was a sacred pact he made with himself, and he broke frequently. But despite his transgressions he also had a drink on the days he was reborn. And it always seemed sweeter on these days, maybe because it was the first time these lips would taste it. [PARAGRAPH]There it sat on a random end table set in the throne room. A bottle and a single glass next to a large mirror. But first, some voice within his mind reminded him, he had a task to do. [PARAGRAPH]Turning he saw himself sitting on the gilded bench he was currently using as a throne. Well, what he knew himself to be. An old man with milky eyes and deep wrinkles in his face. His skin would be splotchy and discolored if not for the unevenly applied white paste all over it. His clothes were bright and new, he had just picked them out for today. The colorful harlequin's crown he normally wore was sitting beside him on the bench, leaving his thinning unruly hair poking unevenly up about his head. [PARAGRAPH]I thought the voices would go with you? the old clown said. I thought I could rest, but they are still here. I don't think it worked, I haven't changed at all. [PARAGRAPH]Really? the reborn Perpentach said as he admired himself in the mirror. He was all lean muscle and confidence. He must have had a beard because even through the white paste he also wore, he could see the bloodied cuts from shaving, some of which had reopened and bled down his face from the laughter. [PARAGRAPH]Yes, I am still Perpentach. the old clown said. [PARAGRAPH]And this made him brutally angry. He was up on the dais like a bear protecting its den. He ripped the old clown off the bench and slammed him easily onto the ground. [PARAGRAPH]Don't kill me! the old Perpentach screamed. I am you. I am Henri, and Pau and Vinner. You will be me in forty years. [PARAGRAPH]The new Perpentach stared down at the old. Had he really been that old and feeble? He thought he had been powerful, the Balseraph court catered to his every whim. But this saggy clown laying on the floor in front of him looked like an imposter in his clothes. [PARAGRAPH]He sat down the old man's chest. The old clown attempted to struggle but was too weak to do anything. He knocked his arms aside and squeezed his neck with his young, strong hands. He squeezed tighter as the old clowns face turned blue, squeezed tighter when the voices screamed for blood, squeezed tighter as he poured all of his self-loathing into his old battered body. [PARAGRAPH]Overall, it was a very cathartic experience. He regretted the fact others aren't able to kill themselves (at this thought they all laughed at poor suicidal Arn). It cleanses the palette, opening the mind to new opportunities and casts off former guilt and doubt. He reminded himself to suggest it to others who looked sad. [PARAGRAPH]And he still had his Blood God wine to look forward to. He poured it, sat in his garish bench throne and propped his feet up on the corpse that lay in front of it and wondered what this life would bring.

Morrigan is served by the Apostasy, an army of worshipers who intend to kill all believers of the old gods and remove any trace or memory of those religions. They are a strong fighting force, but more effective as a spy network as they have thousands of undercover members helping them to find and destroy hidden sects to the old gods.

Oghma is the god of knowledge, in all of its various forms. He is viewed by men as neutral because he doesn't work either to protect or curse men. Only Arawn intervenes in Erebus less. His priests have learned not to expect miracles and rarely if ever actually pray, but they serve him by protecting knowledge and assuring it is not forever lost. Most are librarians, archivists, teachers, and scholars. Many are also mages, as research into the arcane can lead to powers greater than most priests gain through faith. His religion, called the Laeran Cord, was widespread in the Age of Magic and welcome in almost every land. [PARAGRAPH]When the Age of Ice started nations fell to ruin. Survival became more important than learning. The Larean Cord retreated to their cloisters, attempting to consolidate and protect what was already known rather than seeking out new knowledge. The Doviello took particular delight in finding and burning their hidden libraries. [PARAGRAPH]The goddess Ceridwen had Oghma's archangel Embarr torn into three parts; his flesh, his mind and his soul were separated from each other and scattered across creation. The Laraen Cord dwindled to just a single Hierophant, now the high priest of his religion by default. Akharien means "the last one". A scholar with nothing but a frozen world to study, a teacher without anyone to teach. He wasn't that old. He was born during the Age of Ice, so he never saw the world outside of what he read of in the libraries books. [PARAGRAPH]In time hunting parties didn't return. Some priests went mad. Others died of starvation or age. And only he was left. When the Doviello came for him they offered him the chance to flee into the wilderness, to survive as a wolf so that one day he could hunt with them. But he threw himself on the books instead. He begged them to burn him instead of the books. He promised to tell them the stories contained within, and to teach them about the medicinal uses of the few plants that survived in the region. [PARAGRAPH]They didn't accept his offer. He was burned within his library. He was the last priest of the Laeran Cord of his Age. [PARAGRAPH]After his death the man's spirit didn't pass on to Oghma's vault. Instead he remained in the ruins of his library among the fluttering ashes of the brunt books. In death he had more power than in life and the Doviello learned to avoid the place. But others that came and slept nearby would dream of other places and other times. They would hear stories and be inspired. [PARAGRAPH]Early in the Age of Rebirth the Laeran Cord was refounded. A new Hierophant sought out this library and found its meager ruins. The only thing of value that he found within was the high priests crown, which he took to bring to the current church so that it could serve Oghma again.

The Chainbreakers worship an evil goddess in a way that is not so evil. They believe she wants to free everyone from all forms of oppression and non-consensual relationships. They are radical abolitionists who are glad to harbor runaway slaves but prefer arming them to help them kill their masters and free their fellows.

Chainbreakers cannot be trained by those running the Slavery civic. They will rebel against any leader who adopts Slavery. They will target Slaves first in stacks of stronger units, and will transform any slaves they capture into more Chainbreakers

The Emrys are Cultists of Ceridwen who thrive among the Sheaim. While the Chainbreakers' devotion to Ceridwen is often turned to noble ends (like ending slavery and overturning unjust regimes), the Emrys are utterly evil. Their only goals are gaining power and ending the world. They send missionaries to all nations with the aim of seducing talented adepts with the lure of access to forbidden knowledge and powers unseen since the fall of Patria.

A schism occurred among the Brotherhood of Wardens when the cult spread to the Calabim. The orthodox Wardens preached Sirona's command that compassion requires taking action to defend and protect the weak. They tried to raise a rebellion, but were brutally crushed. The surviving sect still professes devotion to Sirona, but promulgated dogmas more in line with beliefs of Pelian the Suffering. Regardless of what evils their inaction might permit, they could not accept that committing violence against others is ever a lesser evil. Seeing too many problems they could not hope to fix, they gouged their own eyes out. These Blinded Brothers have dedicated themselves to providing spiritual care for the weak, in lieu of any material assistance. They mean to reduce suffering, and believe that can be best accomplished by accepting subjugation. They advise those they tend to to embrace their roles, to serve Alexis and the Calabim elite. The Blinded Brotherhood are rare but treated with some respect by all levels of Calabim society. The slaves revere them and devotedly listen to their words, even if they aren't religious. The scourge, taskmasters and middle society of the Calabim respect the Brotherhood and may seek them for words of comfort or advice (though often in secret). And the vampires often act as if they don't exist, allowing the Brotherhood to go about completely unhindered or bothered. Many suspect that when they Brotherhood took their own eyes they also took away the Vampires' ability to see them.

The greatest healers in the world are to be found among the ranks of the Unblemished's Hospitallers, the priests of the Risen Sucellus. Many devote their lives to studying all the most advanced healing arts known to the Ordine Medicos, despite the fact that any placebos administered by hands that the God of Life has blessed is more effective than the best drugs devised by secular alchemists.

The High Priests of Tali can not we weighed down with such concerns as organizing any church hierarchy. Lie their god they prefer to laugh, sing, and dance upon the winds, often calling others to dance with them high in the air.
These high priests cannot only fly but cause all other units around them, friend and foe, to fly with them for a while as well.

Rescuers are good defenders, especially in friendly territory, and can Bless units as well as any good priests. Their special ability to Rescue Refugees can be used to move population points from oppressive rival cities (or your own cities when they are starving) to safer cities where you have more use for them. It transfers a fraction of the city's culture to experience of a Refugee unit, who can turn that experience into culture and production in the city where it settles. All Brotherhood of Wardens clerics can move freely in rival territory and carry Refugees (or other great persons) as cargo though lands you could not otherwise cross. A Devout has a cargo capacity of one, a Rescuer a capacity of three, and a Redeemer a capacity of seven.

Arthendain will can only be trained where the Unblemished are present. He is a healer who is able to cure disease on units in the same stack and is immune to disease himself. More importantly, he targets Mary Morbus and DIseased Corpses in stacks of stronger units, and can attack such plague carriers at a distance to further reduce the risk of your units getting infected.
